CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent fatigue and intermittent chest discomfort.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith is a 37-year-old male who presents to the East Kimberly Saint Kitts Hospital for evaluation of persistent fatigue and intermittent chest discomfort over the past month. He describes the chest discomfort as a pressure-like sensation, occurring primarily with exertion and occasionally at rest. The symptoms are associated with mild shortness of breath but no palpitations or syncope. He reports a family history of coronary artery disease in his father, who underwent CABG at age 60.
Mr. Smith has a sedentary lifestyle due to his teaching profession and admits to high stress levels, particularly during the school year. He has not engaged in regular exercise and acknowledges a diet high in processed foods. He denies tobacco use but consumes alcohol socially on weekends.
He has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He has no known drug allergies.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General: Reports fatigue; no weight loss, fever, or night sweats. Cardiovascular: Intermittent chest discomfort; denies palpitations or edema. Respiratory: Mild shortness of breath on exertion; no cough or wheezing. Gastrointestinal: No nausea, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits. Neurological: No dizziness or headaches.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Chest discomfort likely secondary to anxiety and lifestyle factors. - Recommend lifestyle modifications including increased physical activity (30 minutes of moderate exercise 5 times a week). - Dietary counseling for heart-healthy eating. - Stress management techniques, including mindfulness and relaxation exercises.
2. Lipid management. - Initiate lifestyle changes and consider starting a statin if levels do not improve in 3 months.
3. Follow-up. - Schedule follow-up appointment in 6 weeks to reassess symptoms and repeat lipid panel. - Encourage Mr. Smith to seek immediate care if symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop.
